purpose: Optional explicit gameplay solutions and mechanical altar reminders requested by owner; does not execute or replace learner code

operations.operation: Altar job: Add the shown Wait count, then Shield, Heal, Attack, Attack.
operations.explain: Start with an empty move list for our team. Add the setup's number of leading Waits, then Shield, Heal, Attack and Attack, in that order. Save the finished move list. The power and target lists are independent: filling the move list does not move their entries. A runs your current altar code; this is the job to write.

provenance.adaptation: Owner-requested mechanical reminder of the existing handler; new game-specific wording, not quoted source text

operations.operation: Altar job: Get the marked enemy list character and freeze it.
operations.explain: Get the character stored at the marked enemy list position, then give that character to freeze. Getting an entry reads it without removing it or shifting the enemy list. Freezing stops that character from casting; it can still be targeted. The marked position belongs to this setup; moving the viewing selector does not change it. A runs your current altar code; this is the job to write.

provenance.adaptation: Owner-requested mechanical reminder of the existing handler; new game-specific wording, not quoted source text

operations.operation: Altar job: Set the marked enemy move to Wait.
operations.explain: Replace the move at the marked enemy position with Wait, then save enemy moves. Setting an entry keeps the list the same length and leaves every other move in place. Moves, powers and targets are three independent lists: no power or target moves with this replacement. A runs your current altar code; this is the job to write.

provenance.adaptation: Owner-requested mechanical reminder of the existing handler; new game-specific wording, not quoted source text

operations.operation: Altar job: Add Attack to the end of our moves.
operations.explain: Append means add one entry after the current last entry. Add Attack to the end of our moves and save that list. Earlier moves keep their positions. Moves, powers and targets are independent lists: the new Attack uses the power and target already waiting at its new position. A runs your current altar code; this is the job to write.

provenance.adaptation: Owner-requested mechanical reminder of the existing handler; new game-specific wording, not quoted source text

operations.operation: Altar job: Insert Shield before the marked our team move.
operations.explain: Insert Shield at the marked position in our moves, then save the list. The old move at that position and all later moves shift one place toward the end; the list grows by one. Powers and targets are separate lists and stay still. Shield therefore uses the power already at the insertion position. A runs your current altar code; this is the job to write.

provenance.adaptation: Owner-requested mechanical reminder of the existing handler; new game-specific wording, not quoted source text

operations.operation: Altar job: Add Wait to the front of enemy moves.
operations.explain: Prepend means add a new first entry. Add Wait to the front of enemy moves and save the list. Every old enemy move shifts one place toward the end. Enemy powers and targets are independent lists and stay still, so the shifted moves use different positions in those lists. A runs your current altar code; this is the job to write.

provenance.adaptation: Owner-requested mechanical reminder of the existing handler; new game-specific wording, not quoted source text

operations.operation: Altar job: Remove the marked enemy Shield.
operations.explain: Remove the enemy move at the marked position and save the shorter list. Discard the removed move. Every later move shifts one place toward the front. Enemy moves, powers and targets are independent lists: removing a move leaves every power and target where it was. A runs your current altar code; this is the job to write.

provenance.adaptation: Owner-requested mechanical reminder of the existing handler; new game-specific wording, not quoted source text

operations.operation: Altar job: Replace the last our team move with Attack.
operations.explain: Find the current last entry of our moves and set it to Attack, then save the list. Length minus one gives the last entry's code position because counting in code starts at zero. This replaces an existing entry; it does not append another. Powers and targets stay in place. A runs your current altar code; this is the job to write.

provenance.adaptation: Owner-requested mechanical reminder of the existing handler; new game-specific wording, not quoted source text

operations.operation: Altar job: Remove the first our team move.
operations.explain: Remove the first entry of our moves and save the shorter list. Every remaining move shifts one place toward the front. Moves, powers and targets are independent lists: leave the powers and targets in place. The new first move now uses the first power and first target. A runs your current altar code; this is the job to write.

provenance.adaptation: Owner-requested mechanical reminder of the existing handler; new game-specific wording, not quoted source text

operations.operation: Altar job: Remove the last enemy move.
operations.explain: Remove the last entry of enemy moves and save the shorter list. The earlier moves do not shift. The removed entry is gone, rather than replaced with Wait. Enemy powers and targets are independent lists: they keep their lengths and their entries. A runs your current altar code; this is the job to write.

provenance.adaptation: Owner-requested mechanical reminder of the existing handler; new game-specific wording, not quoted source text

operations.operation: Altar job: Remove the first enemy list character, then banish that character.
operations.explain: Get-and-remove the first character from the enemy list. Save the shorter enemy list, then give the returned character to banish. The remaining enemy list entries shift toward the front. Removing a enemy list entry alone does not remove an character from battle; banishing that same character makes it absent. A runs your current altar code; this is the job to write.

provenance.adaptation: Owner-requested mechanical reminder of the existing handler; new game-specific wording, not quoted source text

operations.operation: Altar job: Find the first enemy Shield and replace it with Wait.
operations.explain: Search enemy moves from the beginning for Shield. If Shield is found, set that entry to Wait and save the list. Finding gives the entry's position; it does not remove anything. Replacing it keeps every other move in place. Powers and targets stay still. A runs your current altar code; this is the job to write.

provenance.adaptation: Owner-requested mechanical reminder of the existing handler; new game-specific wording, not quoted source text

operations.operation: Altar job: Freeze every character in the enemy list.
operations.explain: Go through the enemy list from beginning to end. For each entry, give the actual character stored there to freeze. Freezing stops that character from casting but leaves it present as a target. Keep the enemy list entries: this job visits each character without removing or rearranging the list. A runs your current altar code; this is the job to write.

provenance.adaptation: Owner-requested mechanical reminder of the existing handler; new game-specific wording, not quoted source text

operations.operation: Altar job: Swap the first and fourth our team powers.
operations.explain: First use Roll first power at the other altar. Save the first our team power in a temporary number. Put the fourth power in the first place, then put the saved number in the fourth place. Save our team powers. Saving first prevents one number from being lost when you overwrite it. These are always the first and fourth powers; move and target lists stay still. A runs your current altar code; this is the job to write.

provenance.adaptation: Owner-requested mechanical reminder of the existing handler; new game-specific wording, not quoted source text

operations.operation: Altar job: Roll only the first our team power, from 4 to 9.
operations.explain: Read our team powers. Replace only the first entry with a random number from 4 through 9, then submit that power list. The fourth entry stays put: use Swap power to move the stronger first number there. If the roll is below this setup's needed power, roll again before swapping. Moves and targets stay still. A runs your current altar code; this is the job to write.

provenance.adaptation: Owner-requested mechanical reminder of the existing handler; new game-specific wording, not quoted source text

operations.operation: Altar job: Replace every enemy Shield with Wait.
operations.explain: Visit every position in enemy moves. Whenever the move is Shield, set that same entry to Wait. Save the list after the loop. Keep all other moves in place. This searches the whole list, so it clears later Shields too. Power and target lists remain independent and unchanged. A runs your current altar code; this is the job to write.

provenance.adaptation: Owner-requested mechanical reminder of the existing handler; new game-specific wording, not quoted source text

operations.operation: Altar job: Build our moves: Shield for Attack, Attack for Wait.
operations.explain: Start an empty move list for our team. Read the source enemy moves from beginning to end. For each Attack, add Shield to the new list; for each Wait, add Attack. Save the new our team list. Reading the source does not remove or reorder it. Our team powers and targets remain in place. A runs your current altar code; this is the job to write.

provenance.adaptation: Owner-requested mechanical reminder of the existing handler; new game-specific wording, not quoted source text

operations.operation: Altar job: Move the last reserve move to the end of our moves.
operations.explain: Get-and-remove the last entry from the reserve move list. Save the shorter reserve, append the returned move to our moves, then save our moves. Use the move that was returned: different setups can end with different abilities. Powers and targets are separate lists and stay still. A runs your current altar code; this is the job to write.

operations.operation: Altar job: Move the marked enemy power to the end of our team powers.

operations.explain: Choose a random position from the first through the last enemy list entry. Get the character stored there and give that returned character to freeze. operations.operation: Altar job: Reverse the order of all enemy moves.
operations.explain: Reverse the entire enemy move list, then save it. The last move becomes first, the next-to-last becomes second, and so on. Moves, powers and targets are independent lists: reverse only move names. Their powers and targets stay in their old positions. A runs your current altar code; this is the job to write.
